# Review — cid-tiradas-124-125 (vv. 2543–2617, tiradas 124–125)

Checked: every unit's `t`/`l`/`i`/`n` (30 units) against the pinned packet and conventions.md; the scan, PDF pp. 292–296
(printed 288–292), read on the image, including both tirada rubrics and every Pidal footnote quoted in a note
(2548, 2553, 2564-5, 2569, 2571, 2582, 2583, 2585, 2588, 2589, 2590, 2601, 2610, 2613, 2615), with a zoom-4 strip of
v. 2612 for the italic extent in *espi[di]éndos*. I also checked consistency with the published parts (115-117,
118-119, 120-123 and the earlier parts by search): Ximena / doña in `l`, don Elvira, Ferran[t] Gonçal[v]ez in `l`,
the *en buen[a]* formula in `l` and `i`, *sí vos vala el Criador*, *escurrir* (v. 1067 "escorted" / "saw them off";
v. 2156), *saludar* (v. 2039 "kissed him on the mouth in greeting"), "played at arms" (vv. 1601, 2241), *cavallos en
diestro* (vv. 1546, 2010), *palafré de sazón* (vv. 1987, 2114), *a vigor* (v. 1671), *axuvar* (v. 1649), *fonta*
(vv. 957, 1355), *escarnio* (v. 2464), the lion in tirada 112 and the crow at v. 11. Pass 2 covered all 53 new gloss
entries and the `__broaden__` block, with old entries taken from known-forms.json.

All footnote quotations and both rubrics match the print. The `t` fields joined by "\n" equal the 74 packet verses in
print order (2569 before 2568; 2564-5 one line); no `t` was changed; every `l` has as many lines as its `t` (verified
by script after editing).

## Pass 1: units.json

1. 2545 · l · style. "where [th]ey endow[e]d are" bracketed English letters with no counterpart to Pidal's restored
   *e* of [e]llas and *a* of heredad[a]s (house rule, 115-117 and 120-123 review §5). Now "where they endowed are".
2. 2556 · l · style. "wa[s]" for f[o]: same rule (most published f[o] lines are plain). Now "was".
3. 2612 · l · style. "thei[r]" for su[e]s: same rule. Now "their".
4. 2614 · l · style. "hi[s]" for su[e]s: same rule. Now "his".
5. 2615 · l · error. "he who in good[a] girded sword" put Pidal's restored *a* on the English word and dropped the
   house `l` form of the formula. Now "he who in a-good (hour) girded sword" (as vv. 41, 58, 899).
6. 2550 · n · error. "Averes … grandes, the adjective set apart from its noun across the caesura": on the image the
   caesura falls after *grandes*, so noun and adjective are in the same half-line, split by the verb. Rewritten.
7. 2560 · l · style. "Doña Ximena": published `l` keeps lower-case *doña* (vv. 253, 1351, 2182, 2196). Now "doña".
8. 2592 · l · style. "Don Elvira and Doña Sol": now "don Elvira and doña Sol", as in published `l` (vv. 2160, 2196).
9. 2562 · n · style. "the weddings of tirada 109–111" → "tiradas 109–111".
10. 2564-5, 2570 · l, i, n · error (2570 `i`) / weak (`l`). *arras* was left untranslated in `l` ("in arras",
    "as arras"), and the `i` was inconsistent: "marriage settlement" at 2564-5 but "marriage portion" at 2570. "Marriage
    portion" normally means what the bride's side brings — the *axuvar* the Çid answers with in the next line, the
    very contrast the passage turns on. Now `l` "dower" at both lines, `i` "marriage settlement" at both; the notes at
    2564-5 and 2570 say arras is the husband's gift, kept distinct from the bride's *axuvar* "trousseau".
11. 2571 · n · style. "the pronoun after the verb at the head of the clause (after the subject yo)" contradicted
    itself. Now "the pronoun put after the verb, though the subject yo stands before it".
12. 2572–2573 · i, n · weak. The `i` hung *muy gruessos de sazón* on the mules and palfreys ("sturdy and in prime
    condition"), while the note said the line "runs on to the warhorses". Pidal points a comma after *palafrés* and
    nothing after *sazón*, which ties the words to *cavallos pora en diestro* (cf. v. 2010 *cavallos en diestro,
    gruessos e corredores*). The `i` now follows Pidal ("and warhorses to be led at the right hand, very stout and in
    their prime, strong and swift"); the note now gives the other attachment (the formula *palafré de sazón*, vv. 1987,
    2114) and calls the point uncertain. `l` unchanged (it keeps the word order).
13. 2581 · i · weak. "Serve my daughters well" added a "well" the line does not have (it comes only in 2582). Removed.
14. 2596 · l · weak. "before us you-are both" added an "us" that is not in *delant sodes amos*. Now "in-front you-are
    both" (the `i` keeps "here before us").
15. 2603 · i · style. *el Criador vos vala* was "may the Creator keep you"; the house *valer* in this formula is "help"
    (sí vos vala el Criador "so may the Creator help you", used three times in this part). Now "may the Creator help
    you".
16. 2612 · n · weak. The note made *su[e]s compañas* "the Çid's household", while the `l` said "their". The form does
    not decide between the ladies' people and the Çid's. Rewritten: "'their' (the ladies') or 'his' (the Çid's), the
    form does not say; … the household the Infantes leave behind".
17. 2613 · l · style. "the huerta of Valencia" left the word untranslated in `l`. Now "the garden-plain" (as the `i`
    and the note).

Checked and confirmed, no change:
- **2572 *darvos e***: the split future with *e* = *he* 'I will' is right. The same speech has *Darvos he* (2568) and
  *darvos he* (2575), and the known glossary entry for *e* already records *darvos e* 'I will give you'. Read as 'and',
  the infinitive *darvos* would hang on *quiéroles* (with a clash of *les* and *vos*). The note gives the 'and' reading
  as possible and the form as uncertain, which is enough.
- ***Nos*** at 2569 and 2617 = *non + se*, and at 2549 the subject pronoun: the three notes say this correctly.
- **The drafter's renderings**, all accepted: *Grandes son las nuevas* "a great stir" (Pidal 'gran actividad o animación
  hay'); *escurrir* "escort" in `l`, "see off" in `i` (as v. 1067); *mandar* "bestow" (Pidal 'ofreció en don');
  *saludar* "kiss" (Pidal 'las besó en la boca', and v. 2039); *tener armas* "play at arms" (Pidal 'salían jugando las
  armas'; vv. 1601, 2241); *Valençia la clara* "the bright" in `l`, "Valencia the fair" in `i`.
- **Order and numbering**: 2569 printed before 2568 (said in the note); 2564-5 a single line with two numbers (said in
  the note); the new speaker at 2552 opens with —“ as printed.
- **Uncertain readings** flagged as uncertain: the italic extent of heredad[a]s (the s) and espi[di]éndos (the é —
  roman on the zoom-4 strip); [fonta] [mio] one or two restorations; *darvos e*; and now the attachment of *muy
  gruessos de sazón* and the referent of *su[e]s* at 2612.
- **House renderings**: Ximena (title and `i`), Minaya Álvar Fáñez, Fernando González, Colada / Tizón, "so may the
  Creator help you", *en buen ora* formula in `i`, onor "estate", Valençia the great, Doña Elvira in `i`.
- **Remembered translation**: none found. "the very strings of my heart" (2578) is a natural English idiom built on
  the note's 'membranes of the heart', not a recognizable borrowed line.

Refused:
- 2564-5 `i` gives *por onores* as "the lands" rather than the house `i` "lands and lordship". Here Pidal glosses
  *onores* as 'heredades', landed estates given as dower, not lordship held; "lands" is right for this use. Kept.
- 2543 note: "on Lidforss's view (Pidal's note to v. 2553), the other brother takes up the words" at 2552. Lidforss
  does not name the line, but Pidal's own fresh —“ at 2552 marks the switch, so the inference is fair. Kept.
- 2598 `l` "what may-command you" for the future subjunctive *mandáredes*: "shall-command" would be closer, but the
  note gives "whatever you shall command" and the `l` is not wrong. Kept.
- "Infantes" capitalized in `l` (2583, 2587, 2611): published parts are mixed (120-123 review). Kept.
- 2552 note on *ricos omnes* ("the highest rank of the nobility below the counts") and 2573 "cf. Old French destrier":
  general background, not drawn from a translation, and harmless. Kept.

## Pass 2: gloss.json

1. escurren · error. "Pidal 'acompañan al partir'" is not Pidal: his note to v. 2590 has 'despiden', v. 1067. The
   invented quotation was replaced: "they see off, escort a departing traveller on his way (…; Pidal 'despiden',
   comp. v. 1067; = despiden, acompañan)".
2. curiava · error. "he did not trouble himself" missed the sense; Pidal's note gives 'no se recelaba' ('he had no
   suspicion'). Rewritten: curiar 'guard, take care'; reflexive curiarse de 'be on one's guard against, suspect';
   *nos curiava de* = non se curiava de 'he had no suspicion of', with Pidal's gloss.
3. clara · error. "Valencia la clara 'famed Valencia'" disagreed with the units ("the bright" / "Valencia the fair"),
   and the lemma was given in the feminine. Now: claro — bright, fair, illustrious; *Valençia la clara* 'Valencia the
   fair'.
4. enseñar · weak. "old sense" was false (modern enseñar still means 'show'), and "first half of a split future" was
   pinned to this line. Now general: infinitive; also first half of a split future, with the example.
5. heredadas · weak. "agreeing with ellas" pinned it to v. 2545 (at v. 2605 it agrees with *vos*). Now general: *ser
   heredadas* 'to be endowed, have one's estates'.
6. telas · weak. "heartstrings" did not match the units' 'membranes of the heart'. Now "web, membrane; telas del
   coraçón 'the membranes of the heart', what is dearest".
7. saludólas · weak. "greeted, took leave of them" left out Pidal's 'las besó'. Now 'greeted them, with the kiss of
   greeting or farewell', with Pidal's gloss.
8. doblava · weak. "she doubled" pinned the person to this line. Now "he/she doubled, did as much again".
9. tacha · weak. "sin alguna tacha 'without any flaw'" reversed the force of the line (*non … sin alguna tacha*, 'not
   without some blemish'). Fixed, and 'stain on one's honour' added.
10. llevaremos · style. The lemma was given as *levar* for a form spelt with ll. Now "llevar (levar)", noting the ll.
11. arras · style. Pidal's definition (note to v. 2564-5) and *meter en arras* added, with the contrast to *axuvar*.
12. veran, enbio · style. "unaccented as printed" added.
13. oviéremos, mandáredes · style. The future subjunctive glosses were tidied ('we may have'; 'you shall command').
14. retrayan · style. Pidal's 'nos echen en cara' added.
15. cid, espidimiento, penssavan, repentir · style. The cid entry was made general ("spelt without the cedilla where
    Pidal restores the word in italics"); espidimiento got its gender; penssavan got its lemma spelling; repentir got
    *nos* = *non se* and 'go back on'.
16. __broaden__ · weak. Known entries did not cover this part's senses, so four broadens were added (old entry whole +
    " · " + new reading):
    - *mandó*: 'offered as a gift, bestowed', with Pidal's 'ofreció en don'.
    - *nuevas*: *grandes son las nuevas* 'there is a great stir', with Pidal's gloss.
    - *teniendo*: *tener armas* 'to play at arms', with Pidal's 'salían jugando las armas'.
    - *sues*: also 'their'.

The drafter's *darvos* broaden is correct (old entry kept whole). The known *e* entry already covers 'I will' in a
split future (with *darvos e* as its example), and *nos* already covers *non + se*, so the units' readings of 2572,
2569 and 2617 are supported without a further broaden. The rest were checked against the form and found right:
pidamos, digamos, levaremos, valen, valor, escarniremos, enperadores, callar, diemos, avrán, partiçión, diestes,
quiéroles, paños, çiclatones, levades, gallizia, servides, rendré, atorgado, mandavan, hermanas, pedimos, engendrastes,
parió, señora, enviades, cunplir, abraçólas, andad, bendixieron, diéronles and avueros. gloss.json parses; its keys
equal the novel-form tokens plus `__broaden__`, and every broaden begins with the known entry exactly (verified by
script).

Refused:
- A broaden of *fincaron* for 'knelt': the known *inojos* entry already gives *fincar los inojos* 'to kneel'.
- A broaden of *tengo* for *assí commo yo tengo* 'as I hold': the known *tener que* 'I think' is close enough.
